A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GEOBench-VLM and contain readable main text, tables, figures, references, and complete supplementary material. The retained content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original VLM evaluations, including task accuracies, localization and captioning results, and supplementary robustness analyses.

after.justification: V2 reports expanded original evaluations of 13 selected VLMs, with quantitative comparisons and qualitative results in both the main paper and appendix.

M1.justification: The benchmark retains GPT-4o-assisted, human-verified question generation, five-option MCQs, counting distractors at ±20% and ±40%, spatial annotations, and segmentation-mask conversion. The redrawn pipeline and additional evaluated models do not establish a changed proposed method.

E1.justification: The dataset inventory in v1 Table 6 and v2 Table A1 is identical after citation renumbering. Both retain eight categories and 31 tasks, including optical, multispectral, SAR, and temporal evaluation. General aircraft counting is newly included in the summary heatmap but was already part of v1's benchmark.

E2.justification: V2 adds EarthDial, SkySenseGPT, and LHRS-Bot-Nova to the principal comparisons and referring-expression detection, and EarthDial to temporal evaluation. LLaVA-OneVision joins the bi-temporal versus multi-temporal comparison. The density analysis also changes membership: its ten-model comparison becomes six models, retaining four original models and adding LHRS-Bot-Nova and SkySenseGPT.

E3.justification: Caption evaluation switches from ROUGE-L to BERTScore, changing the meaning of the caption scores. The counting-density analysis splits the former ≤10 bin into ≤5 and 5–10. MCQ accuracy, localization IoU thresholds, and segmentation mIoU remain unchanged; numerical revisions alone do not establish other protocol changes.

E4.justification: Most analysis questions are retained, but v2 removes the temperature and single-versus-multiple-run study from v1 S4 and Figures 19–20. It extends temporal and object-size comparisons to additional models and revises qualitative cases, including replacing an aircraft-counting example.

E5.justification: V1 reports repeated sampling with argmax aggregation and displays single-versus-multiple-run comparisons; v2 removes this reporting. Prompt-variance reporting remains. Neither version supplies explicit repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The summary heatmap and Tables 2–3 contain extensive score revisions and additional results. For example, GPT-4o's damaged-building counting accuracy in Table 3 changes from 0.2420 to 0.5667. Caption scores use a different metric and the heatmap adds an aggregation component, preventing straightforward performance-gain claims. Table 5 is unchanged. V2 Figure A9 also changes correctness labels for retained responses, introducing inconsistencies.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theory, theorems, or proofs. The benchmark's mathematical conventions remain unchanged; replacing a standard caption metric does not introduce a new theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a comprehensive geospatial benchmark exposing VLM limitations. The abstract's leading MCQ model changes from GPT-4o at approximately 40% to LLaVA-OneVision at 41.7%, and the stated evaluation contribution expands from ten to 13 models.

C2.justification: The temporal interpretation changes substantially: v1 S5 argues that two timestamps suffice and additional timestamps can be redundant, whereas v2 S4 emphasizes benefits from additional timestamps. V2 also introduces stronger interpretations about weak numerical reasoning, insufficient exploitation of temporal dependencies, and MCQs preventing hallucinations. These change the scientific explanations and qualifications beyond wording.

D1.justification: V2 omits v1's explicit five-prompts-per-task specification for the retained prompt-sensitivity analysis and removes the sampling study's procedural details. Dataset and sensor descriptions, multispectral three-channel preprocessing, and the benchmark access link are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds EarthDial and BERTScore references and incorporates EarthDial into the geospatial-model discussion. The broader positioning against existing benchmarks remains stable. LHRS-Bot's updated publication information refers to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the introduction, benchmark descriptions, model-selection discussion, results, and analysis prose. It standardizes task terminology and consolidates supplementary discussion before the qualitative figures, replacing v1's interleaving of prose and examples.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns the opening overview and pipeline diagrams, expands comparison tables and heatmaps, changes counting-density bars into lines, and redraws the object-size comparison. Appendix examples are enlarged and rearranged with additional model responses, while the sampling plots are removed. These exceed renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: The expanded geospatial-model comparisons make the benchmark more informative, but new reporting contradictions undermine confidence in the revision. Unlike v1 Figure 15, v2 Figure A9 marks identical answers wrong for retained models and correct for added models. Section 6 also claims EarthDial benefits from temporal disaster inputs despite Figure 9 showing a decline. These inconsistencies, together with removal of the sampling-stability analysis, prevent a reliable judgment that the expanded evidence improves overall quality.
